Elena — thanks for the quick flag. We're treating this as P1.

Quick summary of immediate actions we are taking:
- Engineering is enabling emergency burst nodes for ACME's dedicated pool (ETA ~12 minutes).
- We're applying a temporary low-priority rate cap on non-critical endpoints to reduce KV cache pressure.
- We'll fail over a subset of low-importance routes to the hosted pool to preserve critical payment flows.
- Creating RI ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RI-4567 (assigned to Capacity Ops).

I've attached an emergency-throttle runbook excerpt and a small request sample dump that will help triage.

Can you confirm whether ACME can tolerate a short failover to hosted for non-production traffic? Also please share any additional logs (sample request IDs) if possible.

Karthik

Subject: Fwd: High 5xx and p99 spikes on ReservedQPS - ACME — Exec attention & emergency approvals

Team — forwarding the thread. ACME's dedicated pool is saturated and reserved throughput is insufficient; the customer is on a Reserved contract. Impact: production payment failures (revenue-impacting). Current mitigations (see ticket RI-4567) are temporary.

Immediate asks for execs:
1) Approve emergency capacity allocation (burst GPUs) for ACME for the next 24h to stabilize production while we complete root-cause. Estimated incremental cost: ~$12k.
2) Approve a goodwill credit equivalent to 2 days of service if we miss SLA (proactive retention measure).
3) Authorize capacity team to enable cross-tenant overflow to hosted pool for ~15% of ACME traffic until dedicated pool headroom is restored.

Engineering notes indicate a KV cache thrashing pattern — likely caused by an unexpected model rollout at ACME combined with high personalization prefixes. We need a short mitigation window to flush caches and validate a less-memory-intensive quantization profile.

Recommended follow-up: 30-minute exec sync at 14:40 PT.

Dylan
